children: Shares of EyePoint collapsed on Monday after the clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company reported the second late-stage study failure of its proposed Duravyu treatment candidate for wet age-related macular degeneration, or wet AMD.
EyePoint shares were recently changing hands at 57 cents, down 81% after touching an all-time low of 53 cents early in the session.

The Watertown, Mass., company said it will shed more than half of its workforce as part of a belt tightening aimed at saving $30 million a year after Duravyu once again missed the primary endpoint in a Phase 3 study versus the approved medication aflibercept in people with wet AMD, a leading cause of vision loss and irreversible blindness in people over the age of 50.

EyePoint said it will now focus on the development of Duravyu for the potential treatment of diabetic macular edema, adding that it had about $118 million in cash, equivalents and short-term investments as of Sept. 30.
